title: fix: keep FLUX on Vast
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes Replicate from the public `flux` fallback chain.
- Deletes the retired hidden `flux-replicate` registry entry, dispatcher branch, implementation, and pricing snapshot.
- Keeps the existing weighted two-worker Vast pool unchanged.
- Returns a controlled 503 when no Vast worker is available; the removed ID returns 400 and never contacts Replicate.

Tests: 50 Gen routing/integration tests; 332 alias, pricing, and effective-price tests; Gen TypeScript check.

gist.headline: FLUX stays in the garden
gist.blurb: FLUX now sticks to its two-worker Vast grove instead of wandering into a retired fallback path. When the grove is full, the API says so cleanly rather than taking a surprise detour.
gist.summary: Removed Replicate from the public FLUX fallback chain, retired the hidden flux-replicate model path, and made unavailable Vast capacity return a controlled 503 while preserving the existing weighted two-worker Vast pool.
gist.impact: FLUX requests now run only through the established Vast workers; if neither worker is available, callers receive a predictable 503, and flux-replicate returns 400 without contacting Replicate.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden keeper tending two connected Vast-powered FLUX flower beds, with a retired side path gently closed off by a small sign. A cozy terminal can show a simple “503: workers resting” message, making the controlled routing behavior feel orderly rather than alarming.
